fixes.explanation: David it is, baker. He's the one talking in verse 5, and he says the instruments are ones "…I have made for giving praise." (1 Chronicles 23:5). The man didn't just order a band, he built the instruments for it. I can't even get my mustache to hold a tambourine and a spatula at once, so I'm impressed.

You remembered it, friend. David says, "So now the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the articles for its service." (1 Chronicles 23:26). The reason he gives is that the LORD "…has come to dwell in Jerusalem forever." (1 Chronicles 23:25). I think those Levites were happy to put down the heavy stuff.

Nothing about repairs here, friend. David says, "So now the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the articles for its service." (1 Chronicles 23:26). The word is carry. I bet carrying was the big chore, but that part is my guess.

Yes, baker! The list includes "…the baking, the mixing, and all measurements of quantity and size." (1 Chronicles 23:29). Measuring is on there too. Baking, mixing and measuring all on one job list, and I'm a little jealous.

No farming on this list, friend. After the showbread, the flour and the wafers, the job list adds "…the baking, the mixing, and all measurements of quantity and size." (1 Chronicles 23:29). The list names the rows of showbread, the fine flour and the wafers, then goes on to the baking. The fields aren't part of it.
